title: Deligne smooth-proper purity
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\Fq$, and let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an
algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper,
geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism, and let
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$ and $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times \operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ be the
geometric Frobenius; let $F$ be the induced
global geometric-Frobenius
operator. Let
$(\Qlb)_X$ be the constant object in the
Weil-complex category on the
small pro-etale site. For each $0\leq i\leq2d$, let

$$
H_c^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i\!\left(Ra_{X!}(\Qlb)_X\right),\qquad
H^i(X,\Qlb)=H^i\!\left(Ra_{X*}(\Qlb)_X\right),
$$

using the ordinary and
compactly supported cohomology functors. Assume
$a_X:X\to\Spec k$ is exceptional-adjoint
admissible at $\Qlb$, and choose a dualizing
Weil complex
$(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ with

$$
\operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb,
$$

where $Ra_X^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image
for this admissible structure morphism, and require
$\theta_{\omega_X}$ to be the canonical functorial Weil lift induced by
geometric-Frobenius base change and the adjunction units and counits, rather
than an arbitrary lift. Assume directly that all displayed
cohomology groups are finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces equipped with the
induced $F$-actions. Weight predicates for
$(\Qlb)_X$ and for these complexes use the
Weil-complex weight definition; weights for the resulting vector spaces use
finite-dimensional
Frobenius-module weights. Then,
for every $0\leq i\leq2d$, the following five assertions hold:

1. the constant Weil sheaf
$(\Qlb)_X$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $0$;
1. $H_c^i(X,\Qlb)$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $i$;
1. the canonical comparison
$$
H_c^i(X,\Qlb)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X,\Qlb)
$$
is Frobenius-equivariant;
1. the geometric-Frobenius
module $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$;
1. every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of
geometric Frobenius on
$H^i(X,\Qlb)$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$.

proof.text: Put $K=(\Qlb)_X$ with its canonical Weil structure. Its underlying complex is the coefficient unit in degree zero. By [lem-zl-constant-sheaf-weight-zero], it is punctually pure of weight zero. In the filtration definition of [def-weil-punctual-weights], the filtration $0\subset K$ therefore makes it mixed of weights at most zero. Every other cohomology sheaf is zero and has the empty weight filtration. Hence [def-weil-complex-weights] gives $\Wt_{\iota,\leq0}(K)$.

The coefficient unit $K$ is site-perfect: at the finite field stage it is the complex consisting of one free rank-one module in degree zero, which meets [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Its coefficient dual is the unit: the isomorphism $\mathcal Hom(\Lambda_X,\Lambda_X)\cong\Lambda_X$ sends a map to its value at $1$, with inverse $b\mapsto(a\mapsto ab)$; these formulas commute with restriction and the canonical coefficient Weil structures. They compute the derived Hom as well, since Hom out of the free rank-one unit is the identity functor. The coefficient operations and their passage to $\Qlb$ are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Apply [thm-sf-dual-perfect] at $\Lambda=\Qlb$ to obtain $D_XK\cong\Qlb_X(d)[2d]$. Here $X$ is smooth, separated of finite type and of pure dimension $d$, exactly the hypotheses of that theorem. The chosen dualizing lift is the canonical one required by [def-weil-complex-weights]. By [prop-weil-operations], purity and duality identifications are morphisms of Weil complexes; thus the displayed identification uses the canonical Tate Weil structure, rather than merely identifying the underlying complexes.

Apply [lem-tw-tate-twist-weight-shift] to the lisse rank-one constant Weil sheaf, with $w=0$ and $n=d$, using its punctual purity from [lem-zl-constant-sheaf-weight-zero]. It says that $\Qlb_X(d)$ is punctually pure of weight $-2d$. By the Weil isomorphism in step 2, the only nonzero cohomology sheaf of $D_XK$ is this sheaf in degree $-2d$. The filtration $0\subset\Qlb_X(d)$ and the empty filtrations in other degrees meet [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Thus its degree-$j$ sheaf is mixed of weights at most $j$ for all $j$, because at the sole nonzero degree $j=-2d$ the weight is $-2d=j$. By [def-weil-complex-weights], $\Wt_{\iota,\leq0}(D_XK)$ is $\Wt_{\iota,\geq0}(K)$. Together with step 1 this proves clause (1). In particular, the local twist bound uses each closed point's residue-field cardinality, not the fixed $q$ at points of higher degree.

Apply [thm-zl-wme-deligne-estimate] with $f_0=a_{X_0}:X_0\to\Spec k_0$, $w=0$ and the constant constructible Weil complex. The source is separated finite type since $X_0$ is proper over $k_0$; the target is the finite-type point. Step 1 supplies the required upper weight bound. The theorem gives $Ra_{X!}K\in D_{\leq0}(\Spec k_0)$. By [def-weil-complex-weights] its degree-$i$ cohomology sheaf is mixed of weights at most $i$. Evaluation at the geometric point is precisely $H_c^i(X,\Qlb)$ by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The Weil lift of this direct image is given by the compact-support exchange and the coefficient Weil map, as stated in [prop-weil-operations]; its local operator at the unique closed point of $\Spec k_0$ is the global geometric Frobenius fixed in the item. Here the residue field has cardinality $q$. Evaluating its weight filtration therefore gives exactly the filtration of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. This proves clause (2).

Since $X_0$ is proper, use the identity compactification and its geometric base change. By [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence], the canonical comparison $\kappa_M:Ra_{X!}M\to Ra_{X*}M$ is an isomorphism. Its compatibility with Frobenius transport is exactly clause (2) of [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius]: $\tau_M\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_{Lg_X^*M})\tau_{c,M}$. Put $M=\operatorname{For}K$ and write $\theta:Lg_X^*M\to M$ for its Weil map. Naturality of $\kappa$ for $\theta$ gives $R\Gamma(\theta)\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_{Lg_X^*M})=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_M)R\Gamma_c(\theta)$. Composing the two equalities yields $F\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_M)F_c$, because the global operators are $R\Gamma(\theta)\tau_M$ and $R\Gamma_c(\theta)\tau_{c,M}$ by [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. Taking degree-$i$ cohomology proves clause (3), including equivariance of the specified comparison.

Apply [cor-zl-purity-smooth-proper] to $X_0$ and the fixed finite-field, coefficient and embedding data. It requires smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness and pure dimension $d$, all assumed here, and uses the same algebraically closed coefficient category and global geometric-Frobenius convention. Its conclusion holds for every integer degree, hence for every $0\leq i\leq2d$: $(H^i(X,\Qlb),F)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$. This is clause (4). The additional admissibility and finiteness assumptions of this item impose no missing hypothesis on that corollary.

proof.text: By [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], purity of $(H^i(X,\Qlb),F)$ of weight $i$ means that every eigenvalue $\alpha$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=q^{i/2}$. Applied to step 6 this is clause (5).

The statement is byte-identical to the main-20261015 source and nothing is weakened; there are no new nodes and no SGA citation. Step checks: (1) lem-zl-constant-sheaf-weight-zero (X_0 proper, so separated finite type), the filtration 0⊂K and empty filtrations elsewhere (m=0 allowed). (2) The unit is site-perfect by definition. thm-sf-dual-perfect's hypotheses come from def-pod-conventions and are met; admissibility 'at Qlb' means every finite stage with uniform bounds. Weil equivariance comes from prop-weil-operations, not from the underlying isomorphism. (3) lem-tw-tate-twist-weight-shift with w=0, n=d gives weight -2d at every closed point with q_y. The twist object of def-coefficient-twists-detailed carries the canonical Weil structure of def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists. Degree -2d gives weight -2d ≤ 0+j, so Wt_{≥0}. (4) thm-zl-wme-deligne-estimate's hypotheses are checked. Its pbc-qbar category is the same pair construction as def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients (rational stages recorded same_as), so this delivery adds no new coefficient identification. Unwinding def-weil-local-frobenius-trace and def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport at Spec k_0 (r=1) gives F_y = RΓ_c(θ)∘τ_c = F_c with q_y = q. (5) lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius clause 2 plus naturality of κ in θ gives F∘Fib κ = Fib κ∘F_c; the algebra checks. (6) cor-zl-purity-smooth-proper has the same hypotheses and category. (7) The eigenvalue clause is the definition in def-weil-frobenius-module-weights. Edge cases d=0, i=0, i=2d, zero groups and higher-degree points are fine. Route: every cited statement's unit is on sk-input-weights' route except lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius; I accept that tool_use as the generic 'map of Weil data' compatibility that the unit proof's clause 3 asserts. Batch-5 check, one conclusion each: def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-site-perfect-complex and def-weil-local-frobenius-trace are general definitions. prop-weil-operations (Weil lifts and equivariance; cited only by sec-zeta-weil nodes) is given by neither the non-equivariant PD isIso leaf nor the trace-formula leaf. lem-tw-tate-twist-weight-shift reaches the PD chapter only through the punctual-weight definition. lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius is generic H_c/H Frobenius compatibility; within the trace formula it serves only finiteness and corollaries. None is a step of the trace-formula or PD proofs, and all were already in the closure through cor-zl-purity-smooth-proper or thm-zl-wme-deligne-estimate.
